releases.name: v0.7.0 — AI Studio 0.2.17, safe body migration, and Twin Sparkles icon
releases.body:
Upgrades the managed Google AI Studio backend to v0.2.17 (`0.2.17-magpie.1`) and adds the Twin Sparkles plugin icon.

- **AI Studio 0.2.17-magpie.1** ([release](https://github.com/BUKOWSKIREAL/magpie-gemini-web/releases/tag/studio-v0.2.17-magpie.1)): based on upstream v0.2.17 (`bd6c40f5f8a3a680a19a1ebff67216298d8bae27`), which switches to native SQLite (`mattn/go-sqlite3`, WAL, incremental vacuum, busy timeout) and adds video inputs, multi-account `authuser` session discovery, dynamic `thinking_levels`, and first-event hedging.
- **Safe request-body migration**: upstream v0.2.17 replaces the plaintext `bodies` table with a compressed `request_bodies` table; `patches/studio-0.2.17-preserve-request-bodies.patch` compresses and migrates pre-0.2.17 rows in a transaction before dropping the legacy table.
- **Dynamic reasoning efforts**: `listStudioModels` now derives model variants from upstream's `thinking_levels` catalog metadata (`minimal`, `low`, `medium`, `high`), falling back to the previous defaults for older external servers.
- **Saved `FIRST_EVENT_HEDGE` preserved**: `FIRST_EVENT_HEDGE` is kept across `.env` rewrites while isolating any host environment variable of the same name.
- **Reproducible CGO builds across builders**: C toolchains are pinned in `lib/studio-release.json` (Zig 0.16.0 musl static on Linux, llvm-mingw 20261020 UCRT on Windows, Xcode 26.3 on macOS) and built with `-ldflags=-buildid=`.
- **Twin Sparkles plugin icon** (#25, #26).

### Upgrading notes

- A running backend is left alone; once it is stopped, the next start installs `0.2.17-magpie.1` and preserves accounts, settings, and databases.
- **Database migration is one-way**: first startup migrates and vacuums existing SQLite databases. Back up the data directory (`~/.local/share/magpie-ai-studio`) before upgrading if you may need to downgrade to 0.2.16.
- First-time download size for the managed AI Studio service is ~30 MB (previously ~25 MB).

Validation: [AI Studio verification](https://github.com/BUKOWSKIREAL/magpie-gemini-web/actions/runs/40816292207) and [PR #27 verification](https://github.com/BUKOWSKIREAL/magpie-gemini-web/actions/runs/40812596486) passed on all five native runners; 207 plugin tests pass; live end-to-end Google AI Studio generation, multi-turn tool calling, cancellation, and auto-restart passed.

releases.name: AI Studio 0.2.17-magpie.1
releases.body:
AI Studio backend based on upstream v0.2.17, managed exclusively by the Magpie plugin.

- Built with upstream's distributor settings (`-X internal/app.version=v0.2.17-magpie.1`, `-X internal/app.managedBy=magpie-gemini-web`). Update checks return local managed status without contacting GitHub; installing an update returns HTTP 409 without changing files or restarting.
- The admin version panel says updates are managed by magpie-gemini-web.
- Command-line build (no `desktop` tag), with CGO enabled for native SQLite (`mattn/go-sqlite3`, WAL, incremental vacuum).
- Safe request-body migration (`patches/studio-0.2.17-preserve-request-bodies.patch`, SHA-256 `4cdafbe2c1fb9c2fa913c15845257e0a16bbfa406fb7dc11d0a5bf1eaaa996a0`): compresses and migrates pre-0.2.17 `bodies` rows into `request_bodies` in a transaction before dropping the legacy table.
- Includes five SHA-256-pinned platform archives, upstream MIT license, checksums, and reproducible build metadata (`-buildid=`, Zig 0.16.0 musl static on Linux, llvm-mingw 20261020 UCRT on Windows, Xcode 26.3 on macOS).

Source: upstream commit `bd6c40f5f8a3a680a19a1ebff67216298d8bae27` (tag v0.2.17) + `studio-0.2.17-preserve-request-bodies.patch`. Go 1.27.1, Node v26.8.2, Camoufox 152.0.4-beta.29. Build instructions: `docs/studio-release.md`.

Validation: all five native runners in [the verification workflow](https://github.com/BUKOWSKIREAL/magpie-gemini-web/actions/runs/40816292207) rebuilt the pinned source, matched the archive and executable SHA-256, installed the real archive with isolated data, verified legacy request-body migration across restart, confirmed managed update status and HTTP 409 on update, and passed the plugin tests with that archive.

These are backend assets consumed by the magpie-gemini-web plugin release, not the npm plugin package.

releases.name: v0.6.0 — Backend 4.26, AI Studio 0.2.16 and a sign-in proxy
releases.body:
Upgrades both managed backends and adds an optional proxy to Gemini Web one-click setup.

- **Gemini Web backend 4.26.0-magpie.1** ([release](https://github.com/BUKOWSKIREAL/magpie-gemini-web/releases/tag/backend-v4.26.0-magpie.1)): rebased on upstream v4.26.0 with the existing optimizations. It advertises account-to-proxy binding, which the plugin now requires before importing a cookie.
- **AI Studio 0.2.16-magpie.1** ([release](https://github.com/BUKOWSKIREAL/magpie-gemini-web/releases/tag/studio-v0.2.16-magpie.1)): based on upstream v0.2.16, still managed by the plugin (online updates disabled). The build now recompresses its embedded web assets with Go's gzip, so every platform reproduces the pinned archives.
- **Sign-in proxy for Gemini Web**: one-click setup asks for an optional proxy URL (blank for none). The new account is bound to that proxy before its cookie is checked, even when the backend's pool already holds other proxies. When a proxy is given, the backend download also goes through it.
- **Includes #23**: slow downloads continue while data keeps arriving and give up only after 60 s without any; `authorize` returns at once while the backend installs; long sign-ins are no longer cut off at 300 s under Bun; non-ASCII data directories, relative `--data-dir`, `--proxy ""` and `HTTPS_PROXY` for `backend:install` are handled. Thanks @Mag1cFall.
- **Setup lock**: the holder keeps the lock fresh while it works, so a download that takes longer than 10 minutes is not taken over by another process.
- `scripts/backend.mjs` accepts `--data-dir=<path>`.

Upgrading: a running backend is left alone. Once it is stopped, the next start installs the new version and keeps accounts, settings and the database. If an older Gemini Web backend is still running when you add an account, the plugin explains how to stop it and upgrade.

Validation: [backend](https://github.com/BUKOWSKIREAL/magpie-gemini-web/actions/runs/40472728547) and [AI Studio](https://github.com/BUKOWSKIREAL/magpie-gemini-web/actions/runs/40472728518) verification passed on every native runner; 201 plugin tests pass; public download smoke test passed.

releases.name: AI Studio 0.2.16-magpie.1
releases.body:
AI Studio backend based on upstream v0.2.16, managed exclusively by the Magpie plugin.

- Built with upstream's own distributor settings instead of a patch (`-X internal/app.version=v0.2.16-magpie.1`, `-X internal/app.managedBy=magpie-gemini-web`). Update checks return local managed status without contacting GitHub; installing an update returns HTTP 409 without changing files or restarting.
- The admin version panel says updates are managed by magpie-gemini-web.
- Command-line build (no `desktop` tag), as before.
- Includes five SHA-256-pinned platform archives, upstream MIT license, checksums, and reproducible build metadata.

Upstream v0.2.16 gzips its web assets with Node's zlib, whose output differs between builders; this build recompresses them with Go's `compress/gzip` (`scripts/studio-regzip.go`), so every platform reproduces the same archives.

Source: upstream commit fd6aab611b52fbfe179fbfc1bf830c4343066e32 (tag v0.2.16), no patches. Go 1.27.1, Node v26.8.2, Camoufox 152.0.4-beta.29. Build instructions: docs/studio-release.md.

Validation: all five native runners in [the verification workflow](https://github.com/BUKOWSKIREAL/magpie-gemini-web/actions/runs/40472728518) rebuilt the pinned source, matched the archive and executable SHA-256, installed the real archive with isolated data, confirmed managed update status and HTTP 409 on update, and passed the plugin tests with that archive.

These are backend assets consumed by the next magpie-gemini-web plugin release, not the npm plugin package.

releases.name: Optimized backend 4.26.0-magpie.1
releases.body:
Ready-to-run optimized backend for **macOS, Linux and Windows, on x64 and arm64**, built from upstream v4.26.0 with `patches/argon.patch`. The next plugin release selects these assets by default during one-click setup.

New in this backend:

- Advertises `capabilities.account_proxy_binding: true` at `/`, so the plugin can bind a newly imported account to a proxy before checking it. The plugin refuses to import cookies into a backend that does not advertise this.
- Rebased on upstream v4.26.0; the existing optimizations in `patches/argon.patch` are carried over.

## Build provenance

- Upstream: [zexadev/gemini-web2api-go@7ce02d8](https://github.com/zexadev/gemini-web2api-go/commit/7ce02d89512058b2bd147fb2dc4e40187f5135ad)
- Patch SHA-256: `bfb08cd4f3d95c7ad9f647d256bb2df7bf07db83a6b381cfea5ab9f833c1287d`
- Go: `1.27.1`, `CGO_ENABLED=0`, `-trimpath -buildvcs=false -ldflags="-s -w"`
- Reported backend version: `4.26.0-magpie.1`
- Included: six executables, patched source archive, `build.json`, `SHA256SUMS.txt`, and the upstream MIT license.

The installer pins each executable's SHA-256 in `lib/backend-release.json`. Existing published assets must not be overwritten because installed plugin versions rely on those hashes.

## Validation

All seven jobs in [the release verification workflow](https://github.com/BUKOWSKIREAL/magpie-gemini-web/actions/runs/40472728547) passed. Each of the six native OS/architecture runners rebuilt the pinned sources, passed Go tests, matched the published SHA-256, and installed and started its real executable with isolated data, including the proxy-binding check. The plugin's 201 JavaScript tests passed. These checks used no Google credentials and made no live generation requests.

## Upgrade and rollback

A running backend is left alone. Stop it before upgrading (the managed process ID is in the data directory's `backend.pid`); the next automatic start upgrades a stopped official backend and keeps configuration, credentials and the account database.

From the plugin directory, with the backend stopped:

```bash
npm run backend:install           # select this optimized release
npm run backend:install:upstream  # select the pinned official v4.26.0
```

The selected channel persists across automatic starts. Failed downloads or checksum verification preserve the existing binary.
